assets: the premise register and its confirmations
the lessons and their hash-chained audit trail
the known-defect registry and the postmortems
boundaries: a session that proposes a premise or a lesson and the gate that judges it
a premise's confirmation and the owner it quotes

threats.statement: A premise is marked confirmed without the owner's literal quote, so a high-radius change rests on a confirmation nobody gave. Residual: the check requires a quote, not proof that the owner said it; the quote is text the session writes.
A lesson or a known defect is edited or removed after it was recorded.
A postmortem names no check that prevents its class, so nobody can tell what closed it.

A lesson, a defect or a premise quotes a secret or a person's data into the public repository. Residual: the secret scans find a secret by its shape; no check finds a person's data, so that half rests on whoever writes the record.
A malformed record makes the readers of the register fail, so the structure check refuses every change.

A lesson or a premise is taken as an instruction that widens what a session may do. Residual: the records are text a session reads; the session's deny rules (production commands, force push, workflows) hold whatever it reads, and beyond them only its judgment and the gate bound what it does.

findings.finding: record_errors checks that a confirmation carries a quote, not that the owner gave it.
findings.reason: residual added; the owner's word reaches the tree only through a session.

findings.finding: No check finds a person's data; the secret scans find secret shapes only.
STD-lessons-vocabulary-errors checks the enumerated fields, not the free text that could carry an instruction; it does not mitigate this. A stronger reference exists: the session's deny rules.
